thread:
ivy: FYI found another copy/paste trap in examples/README: the curl example still uses "--data-binary" with JSON and many folks hit parsing errors when they paste into terminals.

jared: which language? i've been scanning python/js but haven't checked the top-level README.

ivy: top-level examples/README.md. snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --data-binary '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx'
```

ivy: issues: 1) inline key example, 2) data-binary causes shell quoting problems, 3) no mention of CLI/SDK parity.

mona_docs: ack. simple fix: use `-d` or show a Node/py SDK example in the same section and mention REDWOOD_API_KEY. i'll add a note about quoting pitfalls for copy/paste.

jared: also add an explicit pointer: "If you're using command-line, prefer single-quoted JSON on POSIX shells or use @file for complex payloads." saves support tickets.

imy: (typo) ivy: thanks. opening PR to replace inline key, switch to `-d`, add SDK snippets, and add a tiny smoke test that runs the curl against a mock. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/512

snippets-bot: lint check found 2 occurrences of `Bearer sk-` patterns and replaced them with `REDWOOD_API_KEY` placeholder suggestions in PR #512.

mona_docs: added a CONTRIBUTING note: "Avoid inline keys in examples. Use env vars and mention default credential chain for Private deployments." will review the PR now.

jared: can we add a docs-lint rule to fail CI if `Authorization: Bearer` appears in .md files? that would prevent future drift.

imy: opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/502 to add the linter rule and hook it into examples CI.

mona_docs: LGTM and merged. thanks for catching this, ivy. small docs fixes like this reduce a lot of friction for first-time users.
